To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Sr 2 ±  x Ba x Ni 1 −  x Co x MoO 6 ±  δ (0 ≤  x  ≤ 1) are novel anode materials that show promising electrochemical properties for SOFCs.

(1) Sr 2 Co 0.5 Ni 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6 − x and Sr 2 CoNiMoO 6 are promising anode materials for intermediate-temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs) with high power density and low polarization resistance; (2) these materials are stable in reducing atmospheres at temperatures lower than ca. 800 °C, but their stability at temperatures higher than 700 °
Sr 2  −  x Ba x CoMoO 5.5 −  δ anode materials decompose under reducing conditions and thus cannot be used in SOFCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of new anode materials for high-temperature fuel cells.

the synthesis, structure, stability and electrical properties of Sr 2 Co 1−x Ni x MoO 6−x/2 anode materials for intermediate-temperature SOFCs, and with the fabrication and performance of cells based on these anodes.
the synthesis, characterization and evaluation of Sr 2 Co 0.5 Ni 0.5 MoO 6 δ as a potential material for SOFCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sr 2 Ni 1 −  x Co x MoO 6 δ anode materials are promising for SOFC application, while Sr 2 BaCoMoO 6 and Sr 2 BaNiMoO 6 oxides are not.
Sr 2 + x Ba 2− x NiMoO 5.5 O 0.5 are promising anode materials for low temperature SOFCs.
Sr 2 MMoO 5.5 +  δ (M = Co, Ni) oxides are the most promising anode materials among all studied oxides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Sr 2 Ni 0.5 Co 0.5 MoO 6 + Ni anode shows promising properties for SOFC applications, but the stability issues should be addressed before the material can be considered as a candidate for commercialization.
Sr 2 +  x Ba x NiMoO 5.5 O 6 − δ anode materials are promising candidates for SOFC applications.
the Sr 2 +  Ba 2 + MMoO 5.5  −  x  · H 2 O (M = Co, Ni) oxides are stable in air and in oxidizing atmosphere, but are prone to decomposition in reducing atmospheres.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Sr 2 +  x Ba 1 −  x MMoO6 − δ oxides are not suitable as anode materials for high temperature solid oxide fuel cells, although their performance in the fuel cell can be improved by the addition of Ni.
